messages:
arjun-sales: Hi infra — urgent POC ask for BlueHarbor (finserv). Need a Dedicated GPU pool + short-lived API key + VPC peering.
arjun-sales: Details: region=eu-west1, preferred SKU=H100 80GB (fallback A100 80GB). Model: redwood-70b-int8 (quantized). Seq len ~1024, avg session tokens ~700, expected concurrent sessions=12, target p99 latency <=250ms. Window: 2026-04-05 to 2026-04-19 (2 weeks).
arjun-sales: Also need a quick cost ballpark and any enterprise blockers (security questionnaire) we should flag to customer.
maya-infra: got it. couple quick q's — is this steady 12 concurrent or spiky? any burst window > 25 concurrent?
arjun-sales: Mostly steady during demo hours (9am-5pm CET) with two 1-hour spikes that could hit ~20 concurrent.
maya-infra: ok. with H100 + int8 for 70B we still need kv cache memory. rough calc: 70B int8 + KV ~ ~40–45GB GPU memory working set per session depending on caching strategy.
maya-infra: for 12 steady + 25 burst i'd recommend 3 H100s reserved with autoscale to 5 for bursts. gives ~40% headroom for batch/eviction and can keep p99 under 250ms if batching tuned.
maya-infra: sample pool config (for ops ticket):
maya-infra: ```
maya-infra: pool_name: blueharbor-poc-eu
maya-infra: region: europe-west1
maya-infra: sku: NVIDIA-H100-80GB
maya-infra: min_replicas: 3
maya-infra: max_replicas: 5
maya-infra: model: redwood-70b-int8
maya-infra: seq_length: 1024
maya-infra: autoscale_policy: target_concurrency_per_replica: 6
maya-infra: ttl_api_key: 14d
maya-infra: vpc_peering: required
maya-infra: ```
devon-se: fwiw on the model: redwood-70b-int8 will be tight but OK on H100. if BlueHarbor worries about cost, offer redwood-13b-quant as fallback — much cheaper and similar latency for many prompts.
devon-se: also recommend enabling prefix KV cache to reduce repeated prefix work; provide eval prompts to SRE so we can tune batching.
lisa-finance: quick cost ballpark: H100 estimate €8.5/hr per GPU (list internal rate), so 3 GPUs reserved for 14 days = 3 * 24 * 14 * 8.5 ≈ €8,652. Add burst usage (assume 2 extra GPUs avg 4 hrs/day) ≈ €952. Infra + networking + support markup ~15% => ~€11,200 total ballpark for the 2-week POC. we can refine after final config.
lisa-finance: if we use A100 fallback, unit cost ~€6/hr => savings ~20%.
infra-bot: New infra ticket created: INF-2026-4421 — provisioning request for blueharbor-poc-eu. Link: https://redwood.internal/infra/INF-2026-4421
infra-bot: Assigned to maya-infra. ETA first pass sizing: 1 business day.
security-bot: VPC peering checklist: customer ASN, CIDR ranges, contact SOC/team, KMS access pattern. BlueHarbor must sign the minimal network addendum; security review expected (48–72h).
arjun-sales: thanks. i'll ping BlueHarbor to confirm expected spikes and get the network contacts. Can you also enable a short-lived API key (14d) scoped to the pool and restrict to their IP ranges for the POC?
maya-infra: yes — we'll generate an API key TTL 14d + IP allowlist. we can also set canary route: 10% traffic -> 13b fallback for cost testing.
arjun-sales: perfect. also pls include a simple canary rollback (auto-fail to hosted smaller model) in case latency/regression appears during demo.
maya-infra: added to ticket notes: canary 10% -> redwood-13b-quant, automatic rollback on 5xx or p99 >350ms for 10m.
arjun-sales: awesome, appreciate it :thumbsup:
devon-se: happy to jump on a quick call with BlueHarbor eng if they want to share sample prompts — that speeds tuning.
arjun-sales: will arrange. closing loop once BlueHarbor confirms network contact + final expected concurrent numbers.
security-bot: reminder: if they want on-prem/private deployment instead of peering, timeline extends to ~3–4 weeks.
arjun-sales: noted. i'll surface that as an option but push for peering for speed.
maya-infra: will update INF-2026-4421 with final sizing and cost breakdown after we get their traffic sample. expected update by EOD tomorrow.
arjun-sales: great — thanks everyone! :rocket:
